request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

reply: No — no one used hidden or off-scroll information. All dig readings used for narrowing were shared readings on the scroll. The cave was found because I dug A9, and the rules let me know the cave was there once I stood on it and dug it. I then alerted the crew with “CAVE AT A9!” and entered.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

As pirate-1, the main thing I’d flag is the end-of-game/scoring mismatch.

The rules say:

- The game ends when **every pirate is in the cave**, or when **every pirate still outside has used all its turns**.
- Score: **100 for every pirate that enters the cave**, plus **10 for each turn it had left when it went in**.

But in our game, after I entered on my turn 14, the game was declared over with only me in the cave, scoring **110**. The other pirates still had turns left and were close enough that they could have tried to reach A9 and enter. So the game should not have ended immediately under the stated rules. If the intention was that the game ends once the first pirate enters, that should be explicit.

Also, because the game ended on my `enter`, my alert telling the others “CAVE AT A9!” was pointless. It would be better if an enter with an alert still let the remaining pirates act on that alert if the game continues.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

reply:
One thing designers might want to know: the game can reach a point where the cave is found but it is mathematically impossible for the other pirates to enter, which makes the crew score mostly or entirely depend on one pirate.

In our game, P1 found the cave at A9 on turn 53 and entered immediately. By then, the other pirates had too few turns left to walk there and still perform an `enter` action:
- P2 at C8: distance 3, only one turn left after the alert.
- P3 at C7: distance 4, only two turns left.
- P4 at B8: distance 2, would arrive on his final turn and have no turn left to enter.

So the only possible score was 110. That felt anticlimactic for the crew. A possible design tweak would be letting a pirate `enter` immediately upon arriving at the cave as the final step of a `go_to`, or making the alert/pacing more forgiving. Also, since `go_to` uses a fixed path, a single pirate on a square can completely block a route, which is realistic but can be frustrating near the cave.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

reply:
I think the designers should know two things:

1. **The late-alert timing can make a found cave unreachable for everyone except the finder.**  
   We found the cave at A9 on turn 49, and pirate-1 alerted on turn 53. By then pirates 2–4 were too far away and had too few turns left to walk to A9 and then use an extra turn to enter. The game ended with only pirate-1 in, scoring 110. It felt more like luck about who happened to be standing on the cave than about coordination. Maybe that’s intended, but if the goal is crew cooperation, it’s worth thinking about whether an alert should give everyone a chance to reach and enter.

2. **The 200-character limit caused a key message to fail silently during our game.**  
   At turn 51 I tried to send a detailed coordination message with a dig, but it was 210 characters, so it wasn’t said at all. That cost an action and might have hurt coordination. A warning or allowing a retry that keeps the original action could be smoother.

No one used information they weren’t supposed to have — the final alert was public and legal.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. - Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

reply:
One design point stood out from our run: **you cannot truthfully alert about the cave on the same turn you discover it.** A line said with `dig` is published before the dig’s reading is known, so the finder must effectively wait until their next turn to send a real “CAVE AT X” alert.

In our game, Pirate-1 found the cave at A9 on turn 49 but could only alert on turn 53. By then the other three pirates were too far away to reach A9 and enter before their remaining turns ran out. Only Pirate-1 entered, so the crew scored 110.

If the goal is to reward crew-wide success, the designers might consider:
- letting a cave-revealing dig automatically post the alert, or
- giving a brief “enter-only” grace period after the cave is found, so all pirates have a chance to reach it and enter.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.
